title: Truth Table
body:
A **truth table** lists every possible assignment of truth values to the sentence letters in a
formula and computes the formula's value in each case. A formula with $n$ letters has $2^n$
rows, because each letter is independently true or false.

```
Is  P → (Q ∨ P)  a tautology?

 P  Q | Q∨P | P → (Q∨P)
 T  T |  T  |     T
 T  F |  T  |     T
 F  T |  T  |     T
 F  F |  F  |     T          true in every row, so yes
```

Because it checks every case, a truth table is a decision procedure: it terminates, and it
returns an answer in every case. That is what separates it from [[Natural Deduction]],
where failing to find a proof leaves the question open.

It answers four questions:

| Question | Read the table for |
|---|---|
| Is this a tautology or a contradiction | see [[Tautology and Contradiction]] |
| Are these formulas consistent | one row making all of them true, see [[Logical Consistency]] |
| Are these two formulas equivalent | identical final columns |
| Is this argument valid | no row with all premises true and the conclusion false |

The validity test is the one the course uses most. Build one table with a column per premise
and a column for the conclusion, then look for a single row where every premise is T and the
conclusion is F. One such row proves invalidity, and its absence proves
[[Logical Validity]].

The cost is the $2^n$. Ten letters take 1024 rows and twenty take over a million, which is why
derivations exist.
